cards.text: Friend, the word of the LORD comes to a man named Hosea son of Beeri, at a time when God's people have two kingdoms, Judah and Israel. Hosea's time stretches across FOUR of Judah's kings: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah. Israel has its own king on the throne too.

cards.question: In Hosea's day, the king of Israel is ___ son of Jehoash.

cards.text: Then the LORD first speaks through Hosea. Most people's first assignment is a name tag and a password reset, but Hosea's is this: go, marry a prostitute and have children of adultery.

cards.question: The LORD gives Hosea a reason for this marriage. What is it?

answers.text: The land is departing from the LORD
Hosea has been hiding from the LORD
The kings have stopped praying to the LORD

cards.question: After the LORD tells Hosea to take a prostitute as his wife, Hosea pushes back and refuses to go.

cards.text: Hosea goes and marries Gomer daughter of Diblaim, no stalling at all. Friend, I once argued with an oven timer for twenty minutes, and the TIMER won.
Gomer gives Hosea a son, and the LORD tells Hosea to name him Jezreel. Soon, the LORD says, He'll bring the bloodshed of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, a former king of Israel (2 Kings 9:6).

cards.question: Along with bringing bloodshed on the house of Jehu, what does the LORD say He'll put an end to?
On that day, the LORD says, He'll break the bow of Israel in the Valley of ___.

cards.text: Gomer has a daughter next, and the LORD says to name her Lo-ruhamah. The reason, He says, is that He'll no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, that He should ever forgive them.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll have no compassion on the house of Judah either.
The LORD says He'll save the house of Judah. How will they be saved?

answers.text: By bow and sword in battle

cards.text: After Gomer weans Lo-ruhamah, she has another son. I bet Hosea holds his breath for this name, friend, the way I held mine every time that junk drawer slid open.

cards.question: The LORD says to name the boy Lo-ammi, "for you are not My ___, and I am not your ___."

cards.text: Not My people. Oof, friend. That's a HEAVY place to stop, but trust me, this story's not done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "for you are not My ___, and I am not your ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The name of Israel's king (Jeroboam son of Jehoash) is a superscription detail. It doesn't move the passage forward, and nothing else in Hosea 1:1-9 needs it. The baker also has no way to reason to it, so it can only be a lucky guess. The same verse could be told on the story card instead, or the card could ask something the passage builds on.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: "No stalling at all" adds a claim about timing that the text doesn't make. Hosea 1:3 says only "So Hosea went and married Gomer." It says nothing about how quickly he went.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The oven-timer joke doesn't share the fact's core action. Hosea simply goes and obeys, but the joke is about arguing with something and losing. Arguing with a timer for twenty minutes doesn't click instantly, and a stranger would likely say "huh?"

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Two answers are kingdoms (Israel and Judah), but "The city of Nineveh" is a city. That makes it a different kind of thing, and it is easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to fill in the exact wording of a line they haven't seen ("not My ___, and I am not your ___"). No story card has said what Lo-ammi means or set up the meaning, so the card tests wording, not meaning the baker can reason out. For example, "servant" fits the first blank just as plausibly as "people".

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "God" is the only capitalized word among the five choices. That points straight to it as the answer for the second blank.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The closing line "trust me, this story's not done" nearly copies the doc's example line ("Trust me, friend, this story's not done") instead of being Papa Dorin's own line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
